title: Anna Persson, PhD
text:
My research interests broadly concern how vowel systems are shaped and understood — from their acoustic characteristics and perception to the cognitive mechanisms that support stable processing across talkers, and the forces that drive patterns of variation and change. My PhD examined how listeners recognise spoken language despite cross-talker variability, with a focus on vowel normalization as a candidate mechanism for rapid and accurate speech perception; I combined acoustic analysis, computational modelling, and perception experiments to evaluate how normalization affects the perception of Swedish and English vowels, alongside descriptive acoustic analyses of the contemporary Central Swedish vowel space.
I now work at the University of Oslo on the ICONIC project which investigates how iconicity—the resemblance between linguistic form and meaning—can emerge and stabilise in human speech through cultural evolution, using experimental methods to understand how form–meaning relationships arise and persist over time in speech systems.
